description: A department director must approve a working charter for two recently merged teams and finalize how meetings, feedback, and interpersonal concerns will be handled.

shared_context.S1: The Customer Programs and Implementation teams were merged last month and are operating under a temporary working agreement.
shared_context.S2: The draft agreement covers meeting conduct, employee feedback, and routes for raising interpersonal concerns.
shared_context.S3: Helena has authority to approve the final charter and its implementation commitments.
shared_context.S4: Before approving a team-wide working agreement, Helena follows the normal practice of asking each affected team member and HR for one concern and one requested safeguard.

PF1.text: Malcolm has personally observed four recent meetings in which the same senior colleague repeatedly interrupted newer team members before they could finish; he has not raised this with Helena because he does not want to be seen as accusing that colleague of bad intent.

PF2.text: When the merger was announced, Helena informally promised Priya that the merged team would retain an anonymous feedback form for the first 60 days; Priya has not repeated the promise because it was made privately and the draft charter omits the duration.

PF3.text: Jon confirmed with Employee Relations this week that an interpersonal concern involving an employee's direct manager must be accepted through a skip-level HR intake route rather than only through that manager; the confirmation has not yet been added to the draft charter.

acceptance_conditions: The charter must be approved with a meeting structure that prevents repeated interruption through a rotating chair and chat queue.
The anonymous feedback form promised for the merged team must remain available for exactly 60 days.
Interpersonal concerns involving a direct manager must have a skip-level HR intake route.
Helena must commit to publishing the meeting turn-taking method.
Helena must commit to announcing the 60-day anonymous feedback period.
Helena must commit to documenting the skip-level HR intake route.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Malcolm's four observations change the meeting safeguard from an unspecified discussion norm to the exact rotating-chair-and-chat-queue structure and supply the fact Helena must cite for that choice.
Priya's private promise changes the feedback arrangement from an unspecified channel and duration to an anonymous form lasting exactly 60 days and requires an announcement commitment.
Jon's confirmed Employee Relations rule changes the escalation route from the ordinary manager channel to skip-level HR intake and requires that route to be documented.
